rubrics.justification: The response largely matches the provided 3AB grading and image, appropriately describing an expanded blastocyst with a good ICM and looser/sparser TE. Minor overreach includes assigning specific regional localization and discussing debris/necrosis with more certainty than the image supports.
It thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor diagnosis, endometrial thickness, sperm parameters, prior cycle history, and lifestyle factors with embryo quality to frame prognosis.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with a plausible prognosis derived from morphology and patient factors. Minor issues include somewhat confident quantitative adjustments and a point estimate that may be more precise than the evidence allows.

Recommendations are generally consistent with standard IVF practice, especially support for single embryo transfer and routine luteal support. Small deviations include overemphasis on ERA/immunologic workup after failed transfers and some non-guideline-supported adjunct suggestions.
The response gives clear, practical next steps for transfer management, luteal support, post-transfer care, and contingency planning for future cycles, with useful specificity.
